page_title: News is bad for you – and giving up reading it will make you happier

sources.entry: News is bad for you – and giving up reading it will make you happier, The Guardian

summary.title: News is bad for you – and giving up reading it will make you happier
summary.one_liner: Rolf Dobelli argues that news consumption distorts risk perception, harms health and thinking, and that cutting it out entirely makes you calmer and more creative.
keywords: how to stop reading the news
does reading news make you less creative
takeaways: News gives a distorted risk map: dramatic events are overrated and slow structural risks are underrated.
Dobelli claims news raises cortisol, increases cognitive errors like confirmation and story bias, and weakens concentration.
He argues news is a competitive disadvantage and wastes time, so cutting it out is beneficial.
Investigative journalism and long-form writing are still valued; important findings need not arrive as news.
The piece is an opinion essay based on Dobelli's own four years without news; many claims are presented without citation.
summary.summary: This is an opinion essay, an edited extract from Rolf Dobelli's dobelli.com essay and his book The Art of Thinking Clearly. Dobelli argues that news is like sugar for the mind: easy to consume, unrelated to life decisions, and harmful. He covers distorted risk perception, stress hormones, cognitive biases, shallow thinking, time loss, passivity and reduced creativity. He concludes that people should cut off news entirely, while still valuing investigative and long-form journalism. The article relies on rhetoric and anecdote more than sourced evidence, though it references a 2001 study and Warren Buffett.
